speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing; to begin our evaluation, how long do these episodes typically last, and were there any triggers or warning signs before they started?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status (Non-convulsive Status Epilepticus) secondary to Childhood Absence Epilepsy.

I have noted the 3-4 minute duration, the "muddy taste" (automatisms), and the post-ictal lethargy; this presentation is atypical for simple absence seizures and suggests a prolonged seizure state. I will request an EEG to confirm the diagnosis.
